routes.label: Find the base and height using special right triangles

question:
Let \(\mathcal{K}\) be the kite formed by joining two right triangles with legs \(1\) and \(\sqrt3\) along a common hypotenuse. Eight copies of \(\mathcal{K}\) are used to form the polygon shown below. What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_10A_Q22_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The useful feature of the kite is its fixed angles. Each constituent right triangle has hypotenuse \(\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt3)^2}=2\), so its side lengths have the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) ratio. Thus the kite's angles are \(60^\circ,90^\circ,120^\circ,90^\circ\), with the \(60^\circ\) angle between its two sides of length \(\sqrt3\).

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_10A_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(P\) be the inward corner on the left, \(D\) the central inward corner on \(AB\), \(Q\) the bottom vertex to the right of \(D\), and \(T\) the boundary corner immediately to the left of \(C\).

The corresponding sides and corners of the two lower left kites give
\[
AP=PD=\sqrt3,\qquad \angle APD=120^\circ.
\]
Therefore \(\triangle APD\) is isosceles with base angles \(30^\circ\). Drop its altitude \(PF\) to \(AD\). The altitude bisects the base, and the resulting right triangle has hypotenuse \(AP=\sqrt3\). Hence
\[
PF=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\qquad
AF=\sqrt{3-\frac34}=\frac32,
\]
so \(AD=3\). The two lower right kites similarly give \(DQ=QB=\sqrt3\) and \(\angle DQB=120^\circ\), yielding \(DB=3\). Thus \(AB=6\).

To find the height of \(C\), track the direction of \(PT\). The common side of the two lower left kites bisects \(\angle APD\), so it lies on the altitude line \(PF\). The three consecutive kite angles between that common side and \(PT\) total \(3\cdot60^\circ=180^\circ\). Consequently \(PT\) continues the altitude line away from \(AB\). Also, \(PT=\sqrt3\), and the right-angle corner at \(T\) gives \(TC\parallel AB\). Therefore the perpendicular height of \(C\) above \(AB\) is
\[
h=PF+PT=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\sqrt3
=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
The required area is
\[
\frac12 AB\cdot h
=\frac12\cdot6\cdot\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}
=\boxed{\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
